records.title: Trend over time
records.guidance: Prefer a line encoding when the main question is how a continuous measure changes over time. Preserve chronological order and expose exact values on demand.
records.avoid: Do not use a line merely because data has many points; if the x-axis is categorical, choose a categorical encoding.
records.accessibility: Directly label important series where possible, combine hue with line style or markers, and provide the underlying values in an accessible table or equivalent text view.

records.title: Compare categories
records.guidance: Use bars when users compare magnitudes across discrete categories. Sort only when ranking is the question; preserve meaningful ordinal, chronological, or domain order otherwise.
records.avoid: Do not impose descending order when category order itself carries meaning.
records.accessibility: Show category and value labels or an accessible table; do not distinguish groups by hue alone.

records.title: Part to whole
records.guidance: Use a part-to-whole encoding only when the total is meaningful. For precise comparison or many similar shares, a stacked bar, table, or ranked bar view is usually clearer than slices.
records.avoid: Avoid slice-heavy pies and donuts when users must compare small differences or read exact values.
records.accessibility: Label values directly and provide a non-color fallback such as a table or stacked representation.

records.title: Distribution and correlation
records.guidance: Use scatter or distribution encodings when the task is to inspect relationships, clusters, spread, or outliers across continuous variables.
records.avoid: Do not add an extra visual channel such as bubble area unless the third variable materially helps the task and remains interpretable.
records.accessibility: Combine shape, labels, summaries, and a tabular fallback; brushing or hover-only inspection needs keyboard-operable alternatives.

records.title: Forecast and uncertainty
records.guidance: Separate observed and forecast values visually and encode uncertainty explicitly with intervals or bands whose meaning is named in text.
records.avoid: Never draw a prediction as if it were observed fact or hide the uncertainty range because it complicates the visual.
records.accessibility: Use line style and labels in addition to hue, and expose forecast values plus uncertainty in text or table form.

records.title: Sequential flow and drop-off
records.guidance: Use a flow or funnel view only when stages are genuinely sequential and the user's question is transition, conversion, or drop-off between those stages.
records.avoid: Do not force non-sequential categories into a funnel shape.
records.accessibility: Keep stage names, values, and transition rates visible and provide a linear stage list or table.

records.title: Target and progress
records.guidance: When a metric is judged against a target, make the value, target, and direction explicit. Prefer compact bullet/progress forms when multiple KPIs must be compared.
records.avoid: Do not use a decorative gauge when no target or threshold exists.
records.accessibility: State the value and target in text; status must not rely on red/yellow/green alone.

records.title: Platform touch targets
records.guidance: Treat platform touch guidance as platform-specific: approximately 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android are useful baseline targets. A smaller visual icon may use a larger non-overlapping hit area.
records.avoid: Do not reuse CSS-pixel target guidance as if it were native points or density-independent pixels.
records.accessibility: Verify the real hit region, spacing from neighboring actions, and activation with assistive technologies.

records.title: Safe areas and system chrome
records.guidance: Fixed headers, tab bars, sheets, and CTAs must respect current safe-area and system-chrome insets instead of assuming rectangular screens.
records.avoid: Do not place primary controls under status bars, camera cutouts, home indicators, or system gesture regions.
records.accessibility: Check that enlarged text and screen-reader focus do not push controls back into unsafe or obscured regions.

records.title: Dynamic text scaling
records.guidance: Use platform text roles and verify the interface with large accessibility text sizes. Reflow hierarchy instead of assuming fixed-height labels and rows.
records.avoid: Do not preserve a compact screenshot by clipping essential text when system text size grows.
records.accessibility: Essential content and actions remain available at the largest supported text setting for the target platform.

records.title: Native controls and gestures
records.guidance: Prefer platform-native interactive primitives and established navigation/gesture conventions unless a product requirement justifies a custom interaction.
records.avoid: Do not redefine system gestures or make a critical action gesture-only.
records.accessibility: Every author-controlled drag or swipe action needs an equivalent visible or assistive interaction path.

records.title: Interruption-safe state transitions
records.guidance: Rapid interactions may cancel visual motion, but semantic state, focus, and content must resolve immediately to the newest user intent.
records.avoid: Never make correctness depend on an animation-end event that may not fire after interruption.
records.accessibility: Reduced-motion and assistive-input paths must reach the same final state without waiting for decorative choreography.

records.title: Alternatives to dragging
records.guidance: Author-controlled dragging needs a single-pointer and keyboard-operable alternative when the same result cannot otherwise be achieved.
records.avoid: Do not make precise drag manipulation the only path to a required outcome.
records.accessibility: Expose state and destination programmatically, preserve focus, and verify the alternative interaction.

records.title: Long token wrapping
records.guidance: Allow URLs, identifiers, and user content to reflow without breaking the container; make flex/grid text children shrinkable and use safe overflow wrapping when needed.
records.avoid: Do not use aggressive break-all behavior on normal prose merely to hide a layout defect.
records.accessibility: The complete value remains readable or has an operable full-value path when visual truncation is unavoidable.

records.title: Chip and tag collections
records.guidance: Let chip/tag collections wrap before shrinking essential labels. If space requires a +n summary, make it an operable disclosure rather than silently hiding values.
records.avoid: Do not compress labels until they become ambiguous or use inaccessible hover-only disclosure for hidden values.
records.accessibility: Interactive chips expose native semantics, focus, state, and an accessible path to every hidden value.

records.title: Focused controls stay visible
records.guidance: Sticky UI, overlays, banners, and virtual keyboards must not hide the keyboard-focused control.
records.avoid: Do not treat a visible focus ring as sufficient if the focused element is covered by another layer.
records.accessibility: Scroll or offset the focused control into a visible region and test with representative sticky/overlay states.

records.title: Accessible authentication
records.guidance: Authentication should support password managers and paste and should not require a cognitive-memory challenge as the only path.
records.avoid: Do not block paste or password-manager completion merely to appear more secure.
records.accessibility: Provide a non-cognitive authentication path compatible with the product's real security requirements.

records.title: Avoid redundant entry
records.guidance: Reuse information already supplied in the same process when it is safe and appropriate instead of forcing the user to type it again.
records.avoid: Do not make repeated entry a default across multi-step flows when the system already has the value.
records.accessibility: When re-entry is genuinely required for security or correctness, explain the requirement and preserve accessible labels and error recovery.
